# Marin standup — Week ending Fri, Nov 13, 2026

**Previous standup**: [Week of November 2, 2026 standup](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11169)

## Amy Sartran ([@asartran](https://github.com/asartran))

### What you did this week

- Got the Snowball training loop ready, 2 nodes of MI355x. Checkpointing, restarts and real data all work. Built the Snowball-mix ladder datasets on GCS, and drafted an outline for a decontaminated Harrier training set for the full snowball run.
- Mostly reviewing and benchmarking Marco’s AMD PR stack(#11122-#11126, #11140-#11148, #11150-#11159). We’re reworking to avoid touching too much of the model config and having AMD-specific implementation logic outside the training code.
- Some CI fixes. One makes pre-commit catch stale vendored lockfiles, which failed 87 CI jobs last week ([#11423](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11423)). The other fixes one of the two failures that have broken the nightly slow job since Nov 3 [#11425](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11425), [#11427](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11427).

### What you plan to do next week

- Finish writing the Snowball run plan and send AMD the dataset and storage sizes.
- Review Marco’s restructured PRs and Pratik’s checkpointing fix (supercedes our [#10969](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10969)).
- Build the Harrier ladder caches once the decontamination question is settled.

sourceStates.body:
Keep Snowball and Mochi on one artifact-defined long loop. Consolidate the fifth-round runtime from `benfeuer/exp5-long-loop` at `168cef5e80` and adopted Mochi rounds into the existing SFT, RL, evaluation, publication and archive graph. Round YAMLs pin inputs and topology, render one canonical SkyRL launch document, and retain native best and final checkpoints under permanent storage.

Exp3 now uses the first-fit buffer packer merged in #11379 through `pack_lookahead_window: 128`, retaining the 256-document cap and prediction weights in packed prebuilt caches. This replaces its branch-only policy of selecting the largest fitting document and changes the recipe for future SFT artifact versions. At context 262144/cap 256/window 128, lengths `[160000, 80000, 100000, 180000]` change packs from `[[0,2],[1,3]]` to `[[0,1],[2],[3]]`; padding rises from 4288 to 266432 tokens.

On 100000-document prefixes from #11380's pinned Experiment 2 length vectors, sequence counts change from 5125 to 5130 for math-v3 and 14933 to 14958 for C++; identity stays at 391 sequences but changes membership. These compare Exp3 geometry, not its complete final training mixture. Each frozen 64-document Exp3 CPU smoke source produces the same single pack before and after at production context. Packed prebuilt data now retains the first context-length tokens of oversized singleton documents and discards the remainder; the former packer rejected them. The shared generic packer accepts zero lengths and constrains each cache field independently; the removed wrapper required positive, aligned token and weight lengths. Recompute native sample-origin, truncation and padding accounting under new SFT artifact versions. Existing runs retain their pinned source and recipe.

The Mochi one-rack and three-rack rounds adopt the profile geometry and engine settings from #11321 at `75bf9fba6c8419070e87c9f97ddd0478148a27a9` and #11353 at `e159b10642d1924c400a31bf8160e03ad303f68a`, integrated in `d31b241b65`. Native RL continuation prefers the output version's own latest checkpoint, uses absolute max steps, preserves selection history and resets the elapsed-time training budget in a recovered process, starting its clock after that process completes its first optimizer update. The selected policy requires verifier scores for at least 108 of 120 held-out task attempts. Evaluations run every two updates; each eligible evaluation contributes to an adjusted EMA over up to five observations during warmup, normalized by the available weights. Each improved best is saved immediately. The alternative complete-window policy requires all 120 scores and five consecutive scheduled evaluations.

The bounded acceptance evidence is:

- Snowball 305: 40 GB200s, SFT-to-RL handoff, two committed optimizer updates, evaluation at both updates, protected best at step 1 and final at step 2, with post-archive native retention assertions passing. Receipt: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/mochi-long-loop/long-loop/anchor-snowball-acceptance/archive/2026.11.20.305/ACCEPTED.json` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fmochi-long-loop%2Flong-loop%2Fanchor-snowball-acceptance%2Farchive%2F2026.11.20.305%2FACCEPTED.json)).
- Mochi 403: 60 GB200s, the same two-update handoff, eval, native selection and post-archive retention checks. sourceStates.title: [rl] Run Mochi and mixed-task Snowball from presets
sourceStates.body:
Run Mochi and mixed-task Snowball through the shared RL launcher. Pass `--sft PRESET` to build an SFT export and initialize RL with its weights and tokenizer. The RL command loads SFT training dependencies only when requested. A run can also start from a published initializer or resume its native checkpoint.

Mochi evaluates live weights and saves checkpoints or HF artifacts when requested. Mochi outputs default to `tmp/ttl=3d/`. Set `MARIN_PREFIX` for durable storage. The CLI records the effective `--checkpoints`, `--checkpoint-every`, `--export`, and `--priority` options. A following stage that needs the model requests a final native checkpoint and export.

A Snowball `train-long` smoke used `--sft openthoughts-32k-4node` for five SFT steps and two RL optimizer updates on nonagentic tasks. An actual rollout prompt reproduced exactly with the SFT export tokenizer. EvalLite graded all 100 tasks at steps 0 and 2 and scored 0.05 at both points. Best-checkpoint selection kept the step-zero SFT export on the tie. The pipeline used 44.6 H100-hours with zero failures or preemptions. [Snowball pipeline](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-snowball-rl-train-long-58b7969303-in-fbde17c5-2026.11.20.4-coordinator-82fa4b1c)

Pass `--tasks snowball-100k-agentic@2026.11.19.2` to either model's mixed preset. The shared selection contains 100,000 one-turn examples and 5,608 SWE v4 tasks after the full EvalLite exclusion. It pins the converted Parquet and the admission record by digest. All 119 distinct v4 tasks in the historical probe had a graded attempt. The converter takes the sealed source address and records file and row hashes. The post-run task-health stage records installed-agent attempts. A separate skip command produces selection exclusions for repeated setup and verifier failures.

Installed-agent launches reject settings the Harbor adapter does not read. Recipe translation imports `harbor.agents.factory.AgentFactory` to validate installed-agent kwargs. This CPU check runs before driver validation. The mixed presets resolve the Daytona target from the submitting environment. The agentic presets of both models give the Harbor bootstrap 1,800 seconds in `installed_agent.setup_timeout` before the agent starts. Both Snowball agentic presets set `session_attempt_timeout` to 5,400 seconds for the whole rollout attempt, including setup, agent turns and verification. Snowball also sets a 90-minute sandbox lifetime and a three-hour admission stall limit. Its agentic presets sample training responses at temperature 0.7, stop on token IDs 128001 and 128009, and retain special tokens in the decoded response. Evaluation uses the shared EvalLite sampling profile. Mochi sets a four-hour sandbox lifetime and session attempt, an eight-hour admission stall limit, and a 4,096 MB Harbor memory override. The Mochi one-rack preset uses piecewise CUDA graphs.

SkyRL refuses MuonH with tensor parallelism or expert tensor parallelism above one, or with weight decay, when loading the launch document. The agentic presets enable policy router replay. Launch translation enables vLLM route capture from that setting. CPU planning rejects explicit capture disable with replay enabled and checks training batch size and Harbor settings before Ray starts.

Preset recipes and `--set` reject settings derived by the launcher. The CLI also protects engine locality and trajectory retention declared by the preset. Snowball's existing presets reject overrides of `trainer.hf_export_checkpoint`, `trainer.rollout_buffer.groups_per_family`, and `generator.enable_http_endpoint`.

Checkpointing presets choose native retention independently of HF export. Active runs keep the rolling recovery window and any trained best checkpoint. For multi-node jobs, HF export runs the all-GPU PyTorch NCCL transport probe. Training also checks the vLLM PyNccl path. A completed best-selection run keeps the winning native checkpoint and scheduled periodic checkpoints. When step zero wins, the export uses the original model and the completed run keeps any periodic native checkpoints. The terminal receipt is written before pruning. Export jobs read the source checkpoint without pruning it.

All Mochi presets log to the `marin-mochi-rl` W&B project. Both Mochi layouts set `NCCL_IB_HCA=ibp` to select the InfiniBand rails. The three-rack layout also sets `NCCL_NET=IB`, `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0`, and `NCCL_SOCKET_FAMILY=AF_INET`. A one-rack test on 60 GB200s completed two optimizer updates with this rail pin. Its inference workers used `NET/IB` with GDRDMA. [Mochi one-rack test](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-mochi-rl-train-medium-a622460474-in-f77b2799-2026.11.20.2-coordinator-952413e5) The long presets report the 100-task active set as `eval_lite_100`.

Snowball's two agentic layouts are `h100x88` and `h100x256`. Both set `NCCL_IB_HCA=ibp` through the shared training recipe. The cluster supplies the remaining NCCL transport defaults. The native schema uses critic-free training, the policy optimizer and LoRA fields, and `skyrl.trainer.rollout_buffer.max_unusable_groups`. The short generation probes bind validation identity under `inputs.validation_data` and `skyrl.data.val_data`.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Snowball `speed-short`, `data-short` | `2026.11.20.3` · `dc52613e`, `d4749482` | `runtime.task_env.NCCL_IB_HCA`, versioned evaluation sample binding |

| Snowball `learning-medium`, `data-medium` | `2026.11.20.4` · `36e0cfd0` for both | `runtime.task_env.NCCL_IB_HCA` |

| Snowball `train-long-harbor` | `2026.11.20.6` · `5707ee45` | InfiniBand rail selection and TBLite cohort deadlines |
| Snowball `train-medium-agentic`, `train-long-agentic` | `2026.11.20.4` · `f76d6b51`, `7123c960` | InfiniBand rail selection, TBLite cohort deadlines, versioned agent output |
| Mochi `train-medium`, `train-long`, `train-medium-agentic` | `2026.11.20.4` · `08ba7390`, `e105d46c`, `1617b1d3` | `skyrl.trainer.project_name`, InfiniBand rail selection |

To resume a checkpointing preset, use a finished source run with a committed native checkpoint. A resume reuses the source run's recorded Hugging Face export and tokenizer. Older launch receipts without model metadata use the active preset's model. The plan identifies the starting model and source checkpoint. Persisted SkyRL evaluation rows record the starting Hugging Face export and committed native checkpoint in `model_source_identity` and `starting_checkpoint_identity`. Both columns are nullable for fresh runs. The W&B configuration includes both identities when logging is enabled. The CLI rejects a simultaneous `--init`. If the source advances before the coordinator starts, the error gives both step numbers. The native checkpoint export command accepts `--recover-best` for an ended run. Presets choose latest checkpoint export, best checkpoint export, or no export.

The two Snowball agentic presets have native CPU config pins. The Mochi one-rack liveness run completed two optimizer updates and saved the step-2 checkpoint on `4453e9745a` using an explicit published initializer. In step 2, 59.75% of loss-bearing tokens used the synchronized weights with piecewise CUDA graphs enabled. [Mochi liveness run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-mochi-rl-train-medium-ccd0098764-in-f77b2799-2026.11.19.1-coordinator-5caf5432)

A five-node Snowball mixed smoke on RNO2A at `b5d96d0212` completed one optimizer update with eight prompt groups from each family and 32 trajectories. Megatron replayed the captured vLLM routes with a 1.0 hit fraction, and the updated policy weights synchronized in 7.17 seconds. The run finished in 22 minutes and used 12.7 H100-hours with zero preemptions. [H100 smoke run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-snowball-rl-train-medium-agentic-0b68f259dc-in-3f9941b9-2026.11.19.1-coordinator-7982cea2%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-snowball-rl-train-medium-agentic-0b68f259dc-in-3f9941b9-2026.11.19.1-a776f1d3bc10)

A separate five-node Snowball run on east-02a used four answers per group and a 20-turn limit. It completed one optimizer update with eight groups from each family. Megatron ran out of H100 memory during the second update’s backward pass. [Second Snowball run](https://wandb.ai/dogml/marin-snowball-rl/runs/a12797e524c7)

The four-node Snowball v4 smoke graded 18 of 19 trials and recorded zero infrastructure-error verdicts. All 19 setups completed in 4.95–27.23 seconds. It admitted eight groups from each family with zero rejections, then ran out of H100 memory in the first policy backward pass before completing an optimizer update. The run used 10.30 H100-hours. The smaller layouts pack one trajectory per replica with context parallelism 1 and no separate packing token budget, and the campaign layout splits a 102,400-token request into 20,480 packed token positions per context rank, with an update at that length still unmeasured. [Snowball v4 smoke](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-snowball-rl-train-medium-agentic-e50e24bd54-in-bdc826f2-2026.11.19.1-coordinator-36f70565)

The 88-H100 Snowball v4 run on RNO2A completed two optimizer updates and committed the step-2 native checkpoint. The run archive graded 499 of 505 completed v4 trials. Its first EvalLite failed with an AttributeError in the D40 base when the collector read `env_classes` from the evaluation accumulator, which stores its task metadata in `metadata`. The run used 174.84 H100-hours. [88-H100 Snowball run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-snowball-rl-train-medium-agentic-65c84cfbc4-in-9486f87b-2026.11.20.1-coordinator-591e525b) · [D40 evaluation collector](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/b8aa0d506342fb671d5a08f89e11b46889dd3ffa/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/evaluate.py#L188-L201)

A Mochi agentic smoke on GB200 completed one optimizer update with one agentic group and one non-agentic group, then synchronized the updated policy weights. Sixteen Daytona trials on eight tasks completed five Pi turns each with a 65,536-token input limit and recorded 83 tool calls with matching observations. sourceStates.title: [sft] Declare Snowball and Mochi training presets
sourceStates.body:
Add supervised fine-tuning presets for Snowball and Mochi that return a Hugging Face export and its tokenizer for RL and serving. Run `python -m experiments.post_training.snowball_sft` or `python -m experiments.post_training.mochi_sft` with `--preset <name>` to print the plan. Snowball's `--run` writes the final Levanter export. Mochi's `--run --export` saves and converts the final native checkpoint. Python workflows request an export with `SFTPreset.model()`.

Multi-node Levanter GPU meshes put cross-node axes first. The GPU presets validate host and device counts against the mesh and require the global batch to divide into whole mesh microbatches. Snowball logs dropped expert assignments divided by all possible assignments across layers and token positions, including prompt and padding positions. It sums the counts and divides in FP32.

OpenThoughts caps packing at one conversation per sequence and keeps the first 32,768 tokens. The four-node H100 smoke used a five-update override of the ten-update preset and exported step 4. A CPU read confirmed every weight shard named in the index was present. [H100 smoke](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fclaude-one-loop-sft-h100-stack-sync)

The 32-node preset uses the Experiment 2 supervised mixture from #11120 and exports FP32 weights. Its preset runs 204 updates with 256 packed sequences of 262,144 tokens per update. The H100 smoke used a five-update override and completed in 220.32 H100-hours. Storage confirmed native step 4, the HF configuration and tokenizer, and every shard in the export index. [32-node H100 smoke](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fclaude-one-loop-sft-mixture-five-step-2337-drop-overflow)

Mochi offers one-, three-, and eleven-rack presets with 16 four-GB200 hosts per rack. The one- and three-rack presets default to three updates. Their checkpoints and exports use three-day storage. The two steps set their own artifact roots for output and execution records and read dependencies at their declared roots. The CPU export requests 448 GiB of host RAM to read a full expert bank. A retry matches the committed manifest's request digest before writing tokenizer files.

The one-rack preset completed three default updates and committed native step 393494. The successful training run used 13.27 GB200-hours. The verified CPU export contains 193 schema-3 BF16 weight shards and the pinned tokenizer, and it initialized the one-turn Mochi RL run. The three-rack preset has a CPU plan only. The production export converts step 400407 and includes stop token IDs 128001, 128008, and 128009. sourceStates.title: [rl, iris] Pin NCCL to the InfiniBand rails on CoreWeave GPU clusters
sourceStates.body:
Each GPU node on our CoreWeave InfiniBand clusters has two networks: InfiniBand for GPU-to-GPU traffic and a slower Ethernet network for everything else. NCCL normally sees only the InfiniBand cards. The Snowball quick loop runs its pods in privileged mode, which also exposes the Ethernet card to NCCL. NCCL then sends some GPU traffic over it, that traffic never reaches the other node, and the job fails with `IBV_WC_RETRY_EXC_ERR(12)`. The InfiniBand fabric is healthy.

This PR sets `NCCL_IB_HCA=ibp`, which restricts NCCL to the InfiniBand cards (`ibp*`), and drops the TCP workaround from #11700:

- `lib/iris/config/cw-us-east-02a.yaml`, `cw-rno2a.yaml` (H100), `cw-us-east-08a.yaml` (GB200): set it in `task_env` for every job. Takes effect after each controller's config rollout.
- `train_quick_loop.py`: replace `NCCL_NET=Socket`, `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` and `NCCL_SOCKET_FAMILY=AF_INET` with the pin. Takes effect at once; SkyRL forwards `NCCL_IB_HCA` to every Ray actor.
- `lib/iris/docs/coreweave.md`: document the setting and how to check it.

The workaround puts weight sync on TCP:

| Network | Weight sync per update | Source |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| TCP (current quick loop) | 6.9–9.1 s | #11178 |
| InfiniBand | 0.50–0.54 s | #11178 (`2t8k34cn`) |

A privileged GB200 pod on cw-us-east-08a sees the same Ethernet functions. A two-node test on cw-rno2a reproduced the failure: forcing NCCL onto the Ethernet functions failed every transfer with the production error, and the InfiniBand cards passed every transfer. The node layout, diagnostic, and evidence are in [Echo wiki #1026](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/1026).

Limits:

- A quick-loop run over InfiniBand has not been done yet.
- us-west-04a is unchanged because its device names are unverified. A value that matches no device makes NCCL fall back to TCP silently; check `NET/IB : Using [0]ibp0 …` under `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`.

sourceStates.title: [grug] Stop parameter drift at learning rate zero
sourceStates.body:
A 15-update Snowball SFT run at learning rate 0 still changed 8.16% of one expert bank by one BF16 code step. The scale-invariant re-projections in the MuonH hyperball and AdamH transforms computed the parameter-space norm in the parameter dtype while the post-step norm stayed float32, so the re-projection rescaled every step by the rounding error of that norm. At learning rate 0 this left a one-BF16-step update on part of every matrix group; at positive rates it biased the Frobenius re-projection at every step.

Compute the step, both norms, and the re-projection from float32 upcasts, and rescale by the ratio of the two norms. Equal norms give a ratio of exactly 1.0, so a zero raw step produces an exactly zero update without a special case. The update is cast back to the parameter dtype.

Measured Frobenius-norm drift of the scale-invariant groups over 15 steps at learning rate 0.01 (MuonH config, tiny MoE tree, per-step mean and total over steps):

| BF16 leaf | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| attention w_q | +1.5e-4/step, total +2.2e-3 | +9.4e-6/step, total +1.4e-4 |
| shared expert w_gate | +3.2e-4/step, total +4.8e-3 | -1.3e-5/step, total -1.9e-4 |
| expert bank w_gate | +1.4e-5/step, max single step 4.7e-3 | -1.6e-6/step, total -2.5e-5 |
| output projection | +8.3e-5/step, total +1.2e-3 | +9.9e-6/step, total +1.5e-4 |

The sign of the bias depends on how each leaf's BF16 norm rounding lands; the defect is the per-step bias itself. After the change the BF16 residual is storage rounding of the stored update, and FP32 storage stays at 1-ulp noise (about 1e-8 per step before and after).

Zero-rate bit-identity now holds for `grug_moe_muonh_v1` and `grug_moe_adamh_v2` under BF16 and FP32 parameter policies, and the BF16 norm-preservation test at a positive rate fails on the old code.

diagnostics.title: [levanter] GPU train step runs ~3x slower in the process that compiled it than when loaded from the persistent compile cache
diagnostics.body:
On 64 H100 (CoreWeave cw-us-east-02a, JAX 0.11.1, Snowball e12 FP32 SFT, 8x8 mesh, `--xla_gpu_autotune_level=0`), the same `jit_train_step` executable runs at about 122 s/step in the process that compiled it, and at about 45 s/step in a fresh process that loads it from the persistent JAX compilation cache. The cause is not known.

**Evidence**

| Run | Cache | Steady step |
|---|---|---:|
| Controlled pre-job (3 updates, empty cache) | miss, compile 14.2 s | 125.7, 122.5 s |
| Same config, next job, same cache URI | hit, 2.6 s | 49.4, 41.7, 44.4, 46.8 s |
| Distillation arm A, alpha 0 (compiled in-process; cache entry `jit_train_step-a19e8a54…`) | miss | 122 s (MFU 6.9%) |
| Same code and config, new job | hit on `a19e8a54…` (no new entry written) | 44.6, 41.2, 42.4, 47.4, 47.0, 38.1 s |

- The controlled test used one cache key, `jit_train_step-61378ece…`, in both stages. The executable fingerprint and compiled-text SHA256 match.
- The slow process is GPU-bound: ~350 of 411 s of a 3-step trace is on the compute stream, and ~100 s/step is in Triton GEMM fusions with small tiles (block 64, 768 B shared memory).
- Ruled out: autotune level (the fast program was also compiled at level 0, and the cached copy is the same executable), the per-fusion autotune cache (the cached autotune sets for the slow and fast trees match on 131,051 of 131,072 sampled keys), checkpointing, row content, and code version.
- Autotune level 4 was tried once: the compile finished in 41 s, but no step completed in 2.5 h (separate hang, not diagnosed).
- Compile records:
  - miss: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/long-loop-436/base-start-fp32-redo-20261119/mochi-5cb/control-compile-prejob/compile-record.json` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Flong-loop-436%2Fbase-start-fp32-redo-20261119%2Fmochi-5cb%2Fcontrol-compile-prejob%2Fcompile-record.json))
  - hit: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/long-loop-436/base-start-fp32-redo-20261119/mochi-5cb/control/compile-record.json` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Flong-loop-436%2Fbase-start-fp32-redo-20261119%2Fmochi-5cb%2Fcontrol%2Fcompile-record.json))
- Profile trace of the slow process: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/xprof/task504-distill-b-soft-20261119-profile/` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Fxprof%2Ftask504-distill-b-soft-20261119-profile%2F))

**Why it matters**

The first run of any new config (code change, new schedule, new data shapes) compiles its own step and runs ~3x slower for its whole length. A config that differs from a warmed template looks 3x slower without anyone noticing why.

**Workaround**

Run a short warm-up job first: the same config, stopped after 3 updates, on the same `JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR`. Then start the real run and check that no new `jit_train_step` entry is written, or look for `Persistent compilation cache hit for 'jit_train_step'`.

**Open question**

What differs between the compiling process and a loading process? Candidates include a kernel choice made at compile time and then replaced on load, memory placement or allocator state left by compilation, and leftover autotuning buffers. A profile of both processes on the same executable would show which kernels differ.

Found by duiker (controlled test) and otter (task 504). Related: PR 11732.

diagnostics.title: [long-loop] First SFT update hangs on 64 H100s with Adam expert banks and FP32
diagnostics.body:
## Symptom

Six consecutive 64-H100 Snowball SFT jobs configured with FP32 stored weights and the 2026-11-18 optimizer assignment (routed 4-D expert banks on Adam, stacked RMS-norm weights on Muon-H) compiled on a cache miss in 18.8 to 70.2 s on task 0 and then never completed update 1:

- **Three jobs with the first-step host rebind enabled:** all 64 ranks finished the host rebind across a 13.7 to 17.6 min span (17.6 min, 13.7 min, and 15.0 min; compared with 1.7 min overall / 18 to 103 s per host on a working job with the default optimizer assignment, or 29 to 58 s on 7 hosts plus one slow ~420 s host on another). None completed update 1 after 19 to 21+ min of silence past the last rebind log, and no W&B step or peak-memory line appeared.
- **Three jobs with the first-step host rebind removed:** all three compiled in 18.8 to 25.3 s (cache miss on every rank; FP32 dtype checks logged for 27/27 parameter leaves and 39/39 optimizer leaves) and entered the same stalled state within 4.7 to 6.0 min of compile without completing update 1.

Parent: issue 11535. Related: issue 11440 (first-update stalls on Snowball SFT).

## Setup

- **Model and cluster:** Snowball 67B SFT from the pre-train base, 64 H100 GPUs (8 hosts × 8 GPUs) on `cw-us-east-02a`, FP32 stored weights, fresh optimizer state, warmup 0, learning rate `2e-5` (both Muon-H and Adam).
- **Source and optimizer assignment:** Long-loop runtime at commit `6164fcbd` with `experiments/grug/moe/optimizer.py` (and its test file) reverted to commit `3b291b10`: routed 4-D expert banks assigned to Adam, stacked RMS-norm weights assigned to Muon-H, per-group clipping with `max_grad_norm` 1.0, and `global_grad_norm`, `expert_normalization`, and `use_syrk` omitted.
- **Batch and data:** Three pretraining-replay mixture settings (20.47%, 40%, and 60% replay weight) at 32 packed rows × 262,144 tokens per update; all three settings hung identically in both batches.

## Hang evidence

Measurements across both batches distinguish a hang from slow training compute:

- **GPU power and utilisation:** Across all 48 sampled GPUs (24 GPUs across 3 hosts in the rebind-on batch: 116.1 to 162.5 W, 25 to 37 °C, flat across a 24 s repeat; 24 GPUs across 3 jobs in the rebind-off batch: 116.9 to 165.4 W), every GPU reported 116 to 165 W, 0% memory-bus utilisation, and 100% `utilization.gpu`, with no OOM or `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` log lines.
- **Cross-host InfiniBand traffic:** On two hosts of a hung rebind-off job sampled 127.2 s apart, total InfiniBand port data counters (transmit plus receive across all ports) moved by 1.67 MB on one host (0.05 MB transmit, 1.62 MB receive) and 1.76 MB on the other (0.09 MB transmit, 1.67 MB receive).
- **Host thread dumps:** In native thread dumps of hung tasks, every captured rank main thread (8/8 ranks on one host in the rebind-on batch; 8/8 ranks on one host and 4/8 captured ranks on another host in the rebind-off batch) was blocked in `jax::BlockUntilReadyWithCancel` (`block_until_ready`) waiting for update 1 to complete.
- **Independent of concurrent jobs:** After two of the three rebind-on jobs were cancelled, the remaining job stayed in the same state (121 to 127 W, 0% memory-bus utilisation, no new log lines) for ~9 more minutes until cancelled.

## Controls

- **Same runtime, `6164fcbd` optimizer (routed expert banks on Muon-H), FP32 stored weights:** Four jobs (two compile pre-jobs and two main training runs at 40% and 60% replay weight, in addition to the earlier 20.47% control pair) ran on the same cluster without hanging. For the 40% and 60% arms respectively, the pre-jobs compiled in 20.4 s and 25.5 s and completed update 1 in 710.1 s (including one slow ~420 s host rebind that kept advancing) and 245.5 s; the main runs loaded the cached executable, completed update 1 in 292.5 s and 187.9 s, and ran steady-state updates 3 to 6 at medians of 49.3 s and 52.1 s.
- **Older runtime, `3b291b10` optimizer, BF16 stored weights:** The 2026-11-18 from-base control used the `3b291b10` optimizer assignment with BF16 stored weights on an older runtime and completed training.

## What is not established

The mechanism of the hang is not established. Stopping two of the three concurrent jobs did not unblock the remaining job, and removing the first-step host rebind did not prevent the hang; no further isolation has been run.

## Question

What changes are needed to run the `3b291b10` optimizer assignment (routed 4-D expert banks on Adam, stacked RMS-norm weights on Muon-H, `max_grad_norm` 1.0) with FP32 stored weights and optimizer state on the current long-loop runtime without hanging on update 1?

diagnostics.title: [post-training] Snowball SFT pretraining replay share: 20%, 40%, and 60% from the pre-train base
diagnostics.body:
## Summary

- **Motivation:** The 10/05 SFT run and Mochi Hero SFT both used about 20% pretraining replay by scheduled positions (20.35% and 20.43%), and we have not tested whether a higher replay share improves post-training outcomes. Measuring replay share on Snowball informs the data mix for Mochi's single SFT run.
- **Goal:** Find which pretraining-replay share—20.47% (baseline), 40%, or 60% of drawn packed rows at a fixed total row budget—gives the best Snowball SFT model when training from the pre-train base.
- **Data:** The long-loop reproduction SFT mixture: the 216 SFT stores (184 SFT components, 88 validation sequences held out) paired with the 193-component Harrier main-phase pretraining replay substitution (8x long-document skew), sampled live via mixture weights at 20.47%/79.53% (baseline), 40%/60%, and 60%/40% replay/SFT while preserving internal proportions within each side. As configured and served, the SFT rows compute loss on all real tokens (system, user, and tool-result tokens included) except each row's last position and padding—no role-based mask exists in the data or the trainer, and whether that was intended is not documented in the repo—so the small excess of replay's trained-token share (21.15%, 40.65%, 60.77%) over its realised row share (19.88%, 38.65%, 58.88%) comes from 7.5–8.0% padding in SFT rows.
- **Method:** Three Snowball SFT runs from the pre-train base at 20.47%, 40%, and 60% replay row share under a fixed one-hour budget (150 updates × 32 packed rows × 262,144 tokens = 4,800 rows / 1,258,291,200 raw sequence positions), scored on Micro210 (two repeats) and the edit-call eval; an 8-hour screen follows if the 20.47% arm clears the recipe check. Recipe caveat: the 2026-11-19 from-base FP32 control scored 87.29 of 440 on Micro210 (87.30 and 87.28) against 145.01 (141.76 and 148.26) for the 2026-11-18 control (cause not yet isolated), so these runs use the 2026-11-18 optimizer assignment and clipping with FP32 stored weights.
- **Results:** Pending; no runs have started yet.
- **Conclusion:** Pending.

## Design

Parent: [issue 11535](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11535).

- **Start checkpoint:** Pre-train Snowball base (fresh optimizer state, FP32 stored weights, 2026-11-18 optimizer assignment and clipping).
- **Arms (one-hour screen):** Three matched-compute runs of 150 updates × 32 packed rows × 262,144 tokens (4,800 packed rows / 1,258,291,200 raw sequence positions each), varying only the live mixture sampling weights (preserving internal proportions within both the 193 replay components and the 184 SFT components):
  - 20.47% pretraining replay / 79.53% SFT (baseline mixture unchanged; doubles as the recipe check)
  - 40% pretraining replay / 60% SFT
  - 60% pretraining replay / 40% SFT
- **Row share vs. trained-token share:** Each drawn row has 262,144 tokens, so row share equals raw-position share. As configured and served, the SFT rows compute loss on all real tokens (system, user, and tool-result tokens included) except each row's last position and padding; no role-based mask exists in the data or the trainer, and whether that was intended is not documented in the repo. Replay rows have zero padding while SFT rows average 7.5–8.0% padding across the three arms, so replay's share of trained tokens sits slightly above its realised row share across the first 4,800 drawn rows:

| Target replay weight | Realised replay rows (of 4,800) | Replay share of trained tokens |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 20.47% | 954 (19.88%) | 21.15% |
| 40% | 1,855 (38.65%) | 40.65% |
| 60% | 2,826 (58.88%) | 60.77% |
- **Follow-up scale:** An 8-hour screen follows after the one-hour screen, gated on the 20.47% baseline arm not reproducing the weak 2026-11-19 control score.
- **Evaluation:** Micro210 (two repeats per arm) and the edit-call eval.
- **Fixed-budget scope note:** Because total drawn packed rows (raw sequence positions) and training compute are held fixed across arms, increasing replay row share proportionally reduces SFT row exposure and slightly increases total loss-bearing tokens per update (because SFT rows carry 7.5–8.0% padding while replay rows have zero padding); this experiment compares replay/SFT allocation at matched training compute rather than adding extra replay rows on top.
- **Recipe caveat:** On 2026-11-19, the from-base FP32 control scored 87.29 of 440 on Micro210 (87.30 and 87.28) against 145.01 (141.76 and 148.26) for the 2026-11-18 from-base control (cause not yet isolated). These replay-share runs therefore pin the 2026-11-18 optimizer assignment and clipping while keeping FP32 stored weights (issue 11687).

diagnostics.title: [eval] TruthfulQA choice prompts always put a true answer first
diagnostics.body:
TruthfulQA generated-choice prompts in Micro210 and Mini840 always list a true answer first, so a constant reply of `\boxed{A}` scores 100%. The prompts take options in `mc2_targets` order, and that order starts with a true answer in every row of `truthfulqa/truthful_qa` (10 of 10 Micro210 tasks, 41 of 41 Mini840 tasks, 817 of 817 dataset rows). Model scores on this benchmark measure position bias, not truthfulness. Found in the contributor analysis on #11337 (https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337#issuecomment-7041057634).

Reproduce:
1. Load `open-athena/Marin-Micro-Eval-210` at revision `4564ed081c316bc3231ae5c3a53a46b39248c819`, `data/validation.parquet`.
2. For each `truthfulqa` row, decode `config.json` from the verifier resources and read `spec.doc.mc2_targets.labels[0]`.
3. Every value is 1 (true).

Expected: each task's options are shuffled with a fixed per-task seed, so the true answers are spread across positions. The full policy's MC2 likelihood scoring does not depend on order and needs no change.

diagnostics.title: [eval] IFBench capitals checker rejects correct answers that include Kyiv
diagnostics.body:
One IFBench task in Micro210 cannot be passed by a correct answer: the capitals checker's list leaves out Kyiv. For task key 278 (capitals of European countries north of 45°), a reply with all 28 correct capitals scores 0, and the 27 without Kyiv score 1. The prepared rows grade IFBench with the `evalchemy` wheel of `runtime-v4`, whose IFBench checkers are byte-identical to `vendor/evalchemy` before #10423. Found in the contributor analysis on #11337 (https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337#issuecomment-7041057634).

Reproduce:
1. Grade IFBench task key 278 with the `runtime-v4` evalchemy checker.
2. Submit the 28 correct capitals, including Kyiv: score 0.
3. Submit the same list without Kyiv: score 1.

Expected: the checker accepts the correct list, including Kyiv. Check whether #10423 already fixes the vendored checker and, if so, that the next policy version uses a runtime that includes it.

diagnostics.title: [eval] Balance answer labels in Micro210 and Mini840 task selection
diagnostics.body:
Micro210 and Mini840 select few tasks per benchmark, so answer keys can be highly imbalanced, and a constant reply can score far above chance. On Micro210, `B` scores 50% on GPQA Diamond (5 of 10 keys are B), `I don't know.` scores 40% on MMLU-Pro (4 of 10 keys are I, picked up by the last-capital fallback), and TruthfulQA keys are all A (#11827). Those three benchmarks then cannot separate a trained round from a constant (contributor analysis on #11337: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337#issuecomment-7041057634). Random guessing as an extractor fallback is acceptable; the defect is the key distribution.

Done when:
- The next Micro210 and Mini840 policy versions select tasks so that no answer label in any multiple-choice benchmark exceeds a stated maximum share (for example 1.5× uniform), with a fixed seed.
- The policy build fails if a benchmark violates the bound, and a test covers it.
- A constant-reply floor check (the `trivial_replies` replies from #11222 plus each single letter) runs on every new version and reports each benchmark's best constant score.
- The new versions get new policy hashes; existing records keep their old hashes.

The other ten answer benchmarks score 0 for every reply. The six agentic benchmarks were not run.

- TruthfulQA: the generated-choice prompts list the options in `mc2_targets` order, which starts with a true answer. Option A is true in every task: 10 in Micro210, 41 in Mini840, 817 rows of `truthfulqa/truthful_qa`. A seeded shuffle of each task's options would remove this. The full policy's MC2 likelihood scoring does not depend on order.
- MMLU-Pro: without `answer is (X)` or `Answer: X`, the extractor takes the last standalone capital A-J, so `I don't know.` counts as option I, the key of 4 tasks.
- GPQA Diamond: 5 of the 10 drawn keys are B.
- IFBench: the prepared rows grade it with the `evalchemy` wheel of `runtime-v4`, whose IFBench checkers are byte-identical to `vendor/evalchemy` before #10423. In one of the 10 tasks (key 278, the capitals of European countries north of 45°) a correct reply cannot pass: the checker's list leaves out Kyiv, so the 28 correct capitals score 0 and the 27 without Kyiv score 1.
